name: Kolibri 1

lineage.how_derived: trained from scratch (20T pretraining tokens, 3.44T mid-training, 201B long-context extension, SFT and RL); FP8 build is the main repo, BF16 in Aleph-Alpha/Kolibri-1-BF16

purpose: Strong German and English performance at low serving cost: a MoE reasoning model with a tokenizer tailored to German word structure; two languages by design (depth over breadth). Intended for conversational assistants and agentic workflows with human review, RAG, document processing, tool calling (card).

license.name: Apache-2.0
license.notes: Apache License 2.0 text read in the repo LICENSE file: commercial use, modification and redistribution allowed with notice and patent grant.

architecture.kind: sparse MoE, 50 layers, 4:1 sliding-window to full GQA attention
architecture.attention: sliding window 513 (4 of 5 layers, carry the positional encoding) plus GQA full layers, 48 Q / 4 KV heads, head dim 128
architecture.why_this_design: MoE keeps compute per token low while keeping the capacity of a much larger model; the cost is memory. Most attention layers look at nearby text so long contexts stay affordable; positional encoding only in the sliding layers allows extension beyond the trained length without scaling (card, Design goals).

variants.notes: IQ2_XXS 22.77, IQ2_M 28.08, Q3_K_M 37.62, IQ4_XS 43.63 GB; Q6_K about 69 GB and Q8_0 about 83 GB in two or three parts; 10.9k downloads

pc-12gb.notes: 49.76 GB file against 9.6 GB VRAM plus 50 GB RAM budget; experts stream from RAM (~3.5 B active, decode bound by RAM bandwidth)

engine_support.notes: Card lists Transformers and vLLM/SGLang-style serving on 2x H100 class GPUs for the FP8 weights.

benchmarks.name: Overall (EN) vendor suite
benchmarks.variant: FP8 post-trained; same table: Qwen3.6-35B-A3B 71.4, Qwen3.5-35B-A3B 74.7, Qwen3.8-27B 80.2, GPT-OSS-120B 72.3

strengths: German and English focus with a German-aware tokenizer; the vendor's German overall score (70.8) is above Qwen3.6-35B-A3B (67.3) in its own table
weaknesses: 78B total parameters: 50 GB at Q4_K_M, so it needs 64 GB class RAM or a Mac with 64 GB or more
vendor table puts Qwen3.8-27B ahead (80.2 EN, 79.9 DE) at a third of the memory
soft.behavior: explicit reasoning mode and tool calling; benchmark table is the vendor's, with an 'AA-Omniscience index' of -32.8 (more wrong than right answers on that set)
soft.maturity: Aleph Alpha is a German lab and signatory of the EU GPAI Code of Practice; 9.7k downloads of the FP8 repo, 55k of an abliterated GGUF

tona_fit.reason: The only EU-built, German-focused open model of this size with Apache-2.0 (text read) and 3.5B active parameters, which makes decode cheap if the 50 GB Q4 file sits in RAM. But the vendor's own table has the dense Qwen3.8-27B ahead in both languages, so it is a German-quality candidate to test, not a default.
